about: Permesso for four («Quadrilio», Torino 1787, «Del Permesso in quattro persone», pp. 71-74): «lo stesso, che il Permesso in tre persone». 19 cards to each of the four players; the dealer, who holds two over, puts away two. One goes alone against the other three, who count together. There is no draw: one of the two parts must win, and a hand is never replayed «per eguaglianza di punti» (p. 74). The lone player pays or is paid by each of the three, «come fosse egli tre giuocatori in un solo» (pp. 73-74). Two cards are put away (p. 71: «non può scartarne più di due»; p. 79: «due sole»); the dealer's 21 cards are counted from the pack. Everything not written here is as in Permesso for three.

dummett1980.cite: Michael Dummett, The Game of Tarot, London: Duckworth, 1980, chapter XIII «Tarocco in Piedmont and Lombardy», pp. 258-279 (our scan is partial: printed page 268 is missing)

torino1846.cite: L. B., Il giuocatore di tarocchi al tavoliere, part I (Grammatica del giuocatore), Torino, Serra, [1846]

prammatica1846.cite: L. B., Prammatica del giuocatore di tarocchi ossia regole indispensabili per gli amatori di simile passatempo, Torino, Serra, [1846] (separate issue, cover dated 1846, deposited 27 December 1845; reprinted from the same setting, same pages, as part II of Il giuocatore di tarocchi al tavoliere, Torino, Serra, [1846])

count.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 71: «Del Permesso in quattro persone».

mode.source: [D] Torino 1787, pp. 71, 73: «è lo stesso, che il Permesso in tre persone»; the lone player has the other three against him («tutti tre gli avversarj compagni»).

deck.source: [R] Torino 1787, p. 71: 4 × 19 + the dealer's two over make 78; the sum is not printed.

fool_exchange_to.source: [R] Torino [1846], part I, p. 33 (Venticinque for three): «onde chi ha presa o coperta la mano non abbia ad averne danno»: the plain card for the Fool goes to whoever took the trick; Torino 1787, pp. 77-78 says the same of Permesso for five to seven: «la carta poscia del Folle si dovrà sempre dare a chi ha preso». Written here, not only inherited from Permesso for three: the pages of Permesso for four (1787, pp. 71-75) do not name it. Other reading (stood until revision 8): the card goes to the opposing side.

overbid_returns.source: [R] Torino 1787, p. 62 (Permesso for three; the pages for four, pp. 71-74, send to it): the second reading of «dirà subito», carried over to four: the word returns at once to the seat that was overbid, who holds with an equal bid, overbids or gives way. Said of three players; the transfer is ours. Torino [1846], part I, p. 42 (where the word goes round: the reading played) and Dummett 1980, p. 265 (the pair scheme of the other reading) are named at Permesso for three; the pages for this number of players have no example of their own.

replace.what: who has the word after a raise in the auction

hand_size.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 71: «ora se ne danno solamente più dieciannove»: 19 cards to each.

dealer_extra.source: [D] Torino [1846], part I, pp. 40-41: «non se ne scartano che due»; Torino 1787, p. 71: «chi dà le carte non può scartarne più di due».

dead.source: [R] Torino 1787, p. 71: 4 × 19 + 2 = 78; nothing is left over (the sum is not printed).

count.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 71: «chi dà le carte non può scartarne più di due»: the dealer has two over.

count_mode.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 79 (Chiamare il Re, sending to p. 71): «scartansi pure, come ivi dicemmo, due sole»; p. 71 says «non può scartarne più di due». Torino [1846], part I, pp. 40-41: «non se ne scartano che due, perchè due sole ne sovrabbondano».

tie.source: [S] Torino 1787, p. 74: «o l'una parte, o … vincere; non si … per eguaglianza di punti». Of 91 points 45½ each cannot arise: the card for the Fool goes to the taker of the trick (Dummett 1980, p. 267: «since each will have an even number of cards, no draw is possible»); ours: the lone player who does not make 46 loses (the Onoranza only, at 43½ to 45½) and nothing is replayed.

bands.source: [R] Torino 1787, pp. 66-67, 74: as for three (46 wins; 43 to 45 loses the Onoranza only, the line drawn where the payment puts it, see permesso_3) but «non si può mai rifare per eguaglianza di punti»: 45½ is not a draw; ours: it loses the Onoranza only. p. 74 allows no replay for equal points, so the draw of Permesso for three at 45½ is not offered as another reading.

mode.source: [D] Torino 1787, pp. 73-74: «Chi perde, pagherà tutti tre gli avversarj … esigerà il danaro da tutti tre»; the one against all pays «come fosse egli tre giuocatori in un solo».

call.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 72: «Ordinariamente, se non si hanno Donne sole, … chiami Re, o Donne, o Cavalli»; [R] «Donne sole», «Cavalli scompagnati»: a queen without her king, a knight without his queen.

play.source: [D] Torino 1787, pp. 70-71: at four «richiedonsi molti Trionfi di necessità per motivo degli scarti impensati»; the lone player should have both trumps and figures.

left_out.source: [D] Torino 1787, p. 100: «Vola, dicesi del fare tutte le basi»; the stake of a vola is agreed before the deal (p. 21 rule 10).
left_out.why: The book gives no figure and no rule of a vola inside Permesso; a premium of the table, not played.

left_out.source: [D] Torino 1787, pp. 66, 99: the game may be played «unicamente a guadagnar la partita col marcio»; «Marcio, vale posta doppia … facendo o … a cui la partita è fissata».
left_out.why: Two ways of playing (in coins or only for the game with marcio) are named but the book gives neither a line for the marcio at Permesso nor its payment; only the coin game is played.

left_out.source: [D] Torino [1846], part I, pp. 44-46 (pp. 44-45 read on the Academy's separate image of the «pagine mancanti»; also Prammatica [1846], pp. 20-21): the lone player may declare the Bagatto last, played «in tre, in quattro»: «oltre alla Partita gli altri giuocatori ti pagheranno trenta marche per caduno»; failing, he pays thirty to each, apart from the game.
left_out.why: The book of 1787 does not know it (Dummett 1980, p. 267: «also mentioned only in RI»). The engine cannot yet play a declaration by the lone player only, nor a payment that depends on it (question 17); a playable variant waits.

left_out.source: [D] Torino [1846], part I, pp. 43-44; Prammatica [1846], p. 20: Permesso castrato, the pack without 24 small cards; for four 13 cards each, «e lo scarto sarà di sole due carte».
left_out.why: A later custom of 1846, not in the book of 1787 (not in its index; Dummett 1980, p. 267: «mentioned only in RI»). Not played yet; a playable variant waits.
